MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a factor of 30? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 5
   C. 8
   D. 4

2. Round 918 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 900
   B. 910
   C. 920
   D. 930

3. What is the total value of the digit 6 in 8,064? (1 mark)
   A. 60
   B. 6
   C. 10
   D. 600

4. Which of these shows 604 in words? (1 mark)
   A. six hundred and forty
   B. seven hundred and four
   C. six hundred and four
   D. sixty-four

5. What is the rule of the pattern 1,200, 1,500, 1,800, 2,100? (1 mark)
   A. add 600
   B. subtract 300
   C. add 300
   D. add 1,200

6. Estimate 5,064 − 1,927 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 3,230
   B. 3,120
   C. 3,140
   D. 3,130

7. Work out 9,000 − 6,450. (1 mark)
   A. 2,550
   B. 2,560
   C. 3,450
   D. 2,450

8. Estimate 19 × 31 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 6,000
   B. 500
   C. 600
   D. 700

9. If ? × 9 = 63, then ? is found by (1 mark)
   A. 63 × 9
   B. 63 ÷ 9
   C. 63 − 9
   D. 9 ÷ 63

10. What is 84 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 20
   B. 31
   C. 22
   D. 21

11. Chebet writes another set of fractions. Which of these is a mixed fraction? (1 mark)
   A. 2 5/8
   B. 5/12
   C. 7/4
   D. 9/9

12. Change 5 1/2 to an improper fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 11/2
   B. 6/2
   C. 12/2
   D. 10/2

13. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 12 cm
   B. 13 cm
   C. 7 cm
   D. 14 cm

14. Change 5 m 8 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 5,080 cm
   B. 58 cm
   C. 13 cm
   D. 508 cm

15. A triangle has sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 25 cm
   B. 30 cm
   C. 24 cm
   D. 26 cm

16. A rectangle is made of 4 rows with 6 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 20 square units
   B. 10 square units
   C. 24 square units
   D. 28 square units

17. Musa covers a book cover with 12 rows of 9 squares. Which sum gives the number of squares? (1 mark)
   A. 12 × 9
   B. 12 + 9
   C. 12 ÷ 9
   D. 12 − 9

18. One layer of a cuboid has 9 blocks and there are 6 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 63 blocks
   B. 54 blocks
   C. 15 blocks
   D. 48 blocks

19. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 by 3 by 2 blocks is 9 because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What is her mistake? (1 mark)
   A. She forgot the corners
   B. She added the numbers instead of multiplying
   C. She counted the faces
   D. She multiplied instead of adding

20. What is 4 1/2 L + 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 6 3/4 L
   B. 7 1/2 L
   C. 7 L
   D. 7 1/4 L

21. What is 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/2 kg
   B. 5 1/4 kg
   C. 5 kg
   D. 4 3/4 kg

22. How many days are in 2 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 14 days
   B. 48 days
   C. 21 days
   D. 10 days

23. The family eats supper at half past seven at night. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 7:30 noon
   B. 7:03 p.m.
   C. 7:30 a.m.
   D. 7:30 p.m.

24. What is 2 h 45 min + 1 h 30 min? (1 mark)
   A. 4 h 25 min
   B. 4 h 15 min
   C. 4 h 5 min
   D. 3 h 15 min

25. How many hours are in 2 days? (1 mark)
   A. 48 hours
   B. 120 hours
   C. 72 hours
   D. 24 hours

26. What is a good thing to do when a shopkeeper gives you change? (1 mark)
   A. Count it to check that it is correct
   B. Leave without looking
   C. Throw it away
   D. Ask for more than you are owed

27. A customer pays with Ksh 200 for goods that cost Ksh 145. How much change should she get? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 45
   B. Ksh 155
   C. Ksh 345
   D. Ksh 55

28. If you face north, which direction is on your right? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. South
   D. East

29. Two lines that meet at a point form (1 mark)
   A. a square
   B. a triangle
   C. a circle
   D. an angle

30. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with two equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 3
   C. 0
   D. 2

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A library had 4,250 books and 1,875 were borrowed. How many books were left? Check your answer. (4 marks)

32. Write 4, 6 and 9 as Roman numerals. (3 marks)

33. Describe how to make a 1/2 L mark on an unmarked bottle using a 1 L container. (3 marks)

34. A trader has 800 eggs. Each crate holds 100 eggs. How many crates are needed? (2 marks)

35. Start at 1,500 and add 1,000 each time to write a pattern of five numbers. State the rule. (3 marks)

36. Add 1 1/4 L and 2 1/2 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

37. A shop sells 3 packets of milk of 1/2 L each and 2 packets of 1 L each. How many litres of milk is that altogether? (3 marks)

38. Write the first five multiples of 9. (2 marks)

39. Explain how you can compare the areas of two sheets of paper without using a ruler. (2 marks)

40. For the number 4,835: (a) write it in expanded form, (b) give the total value of the digit 8, (c) round it to the nearest ten, (d) say whether it is even or odd. (5 marks)

41. Two runners finish a race in 12.4 seconds and 12.35 seconds. Who is faster? Explain. (3 marks)

42. Write 2 25/100 and 5 7/100 as decimals. (2 marks)

43. A hundred square has 60 of its small squares shaded. Write the shaded part as a fraction and as a decimal. (2 marks)

44. Explain why the digit carried from the tens column must be added in the hundreds column when adding 3,568 + 2,276. (3 marks)

45. A water tank holds 1,000 litres. Each day the family uses 125 litres. Write the amount left after 1, 2 and 3 days. (3 marks)

46. A learner writes 5 in the mango row but the tally shows 4. Explain why this is a mistake and how to avoid it. (3 marks)

47. Explain why you should read a measuring jug at the same height as the water. (2 marks)

48. Write 583 in words. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — 5
   30 ÷ 5 = 6 with nothing left over, so 5 is a factor of 30. The others leave a remainder.

2. C — 920
   Look at the ones digit 8. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 918 rounds to 920.

3. A — 60
   The digit 6 is in the tens place, so its total value is 6 × 10 = 60.

4. C — six hundred and four
   604 = six hundred and four. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. C — add 300
   Each number is 300 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 300.

6. D — 3,130
   5,064 rounds to 5,060 and 1,927 rounds to 1,930. 5,060 − 1,930 = 3,130.

7. A — 2,550
   Subtract from the ones, regrouping when the top digit is smaller. 9,000 − 6,450 = 2,550. Check: 2,550 + 6,450 = 9,000.

8. C — 600
   19 rounds to 20 and 31 rounds to 30. 20 × 30 = 600.

9. B — 63 ÷ 9
   To find the missing factor we divide the product by the known factor: 63 ÷ 9 = 7.

10. D — 21
   4 × 21 = 84, so 84 ÷ 4 = 21.

11. A — 2 5/8
   A mixed fraction has a whole number and a proper fraction, like 2 5/8.

12. A — 11/2
   5 × 2 = 10 and 10 + 1 = 11. The denominator stays 2, so the answer is 11/2.

13. A — 12 cm
   Add all three sides: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 cm.

14. D — 508 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 5 × 100 = 500, and 500 + 8 = 508. So the answer is 508 cm.

15. C — 24 cm
   Add all three sides: 7 + 8 + 9 = 24 cm.

16. C — 24 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.

17. A — 12 × 9
   Squares = rows × columns = 12 × 9 = 108.

18. B — 54 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 9 × 6 = 54 blocks.

19. B — She added the numbers instead of multiplying
   Volume = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 blocks.

20. C — 7 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 4 1/2 L + 2 1/2 L = 7 L.

21. D — 4 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 7 1/2 kg − 2 3/4 kg = 4 3/4 kg.

22. A — 14 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 2 × 7 = 14 days.

23. D — 7:30 p.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 7:30 p.m..

24. B — 4 h 15 min
   Add the minutes and hours, then change 60 minutes into 1 hour. The answer is 4 h 15 min.

25. A — 48 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 2 × 24 = 48 hours.

26. A — Count it to check that it is correct
   Counting the change carefully is honest and helps avoid mistakes.

27. D — Ksh 55
   Change = amount paid − cost = 200 − 145 = Ksh 55.

28. D — East
   Facing north, east is on your right, west on your left and south behind you.

29. D — an angle
   When two lines meet at a point they make an angle.

30. A — 1
   Only one fold, from the top corner to the middle of the base, makes the halves match.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: 2,375 books. Check: 2,375 + 1,875 = 4,250.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the subtraction with regrouping, 1 mark for the answer with units, 1 mark for the check.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: IV, VI, IX
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. IV is 5 − 1, VI is 5 + 1, IX is 10 − 1.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Pour 1 L of water into one bottle. Share it into two identical bottles until the levels match. Mark the water level on one bottle as 1/2 L.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for starting with 1 L, 1 mark for sharing into two equal levels, 1 mark for marking 1/2 L.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8 crates
   Working / marking points: 800 ÷ 100 = 8. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the unit.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,500, 2,500, 3,500, 4,500, 5,500. Rule: add 1,000.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for five correct terms (1 mark for three or four).

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Wholes 1 + 2 = 3 (1 mark); parts 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4 (1 mark); total 3 3/4 L (1 mark).

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 L (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 L (1 mark); total 3 1/2 L (1 mark).

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the first three and 1 mark for the last two.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put one sheet on top of the other with their corners lined up. The sheet that sticks out has the bigger area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for placing one on the other and 1 mark for saying the one that sticks out is bigger.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 4,000 + 800 + 30 + 5 (b) 800 (c) 4,840 (d) odd because it ends in 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part; part (a) needs all four addends, part (b) 8 × 100, part (c) the ones digit 5 rounds up, part (d) needs the reason from the ones digit (1 mark for the classification plus reason together).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The runner with 12.35 seconds is faster. 12.4 = 12.40, and 12.35 is less than 12.40, so it took less time.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 12.4 as 12.40, 1 mark for comparing, 1 mark for the correct runner.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2.25 and 5.07
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal. 5 7/100 needs a 0 in the tenths place.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: 60/100 and 0.6 (or 0.60)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the fraction and 1 mark for the decimal.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ten tens make one hundred, so the extra 1 hundred must be counted with the hundreds. If it is left out the answer will be 100 too small.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying ten tens make a hundred, 1 mark for the carried digit being added in the next column, 1 mark for the effect of leaving it out.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: 875 litres, 750 litres, 625 litres
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct amount.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: The number in the table must match the tally, otherwise the total will not add up correctly. Count the tallies carefully and check the total.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mismatch, 1 mark for the effect on total, 1 mark for checking.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Looking from above or below makes the water level seem to be at a different mark, so the reading would be wrong.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying the reading can be wrong and 1 mark for the reason.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: five hundred and eighty-three
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for "five hundred and"; 1 mark for "eighty-three" spelt correctly with a hyphen.
